identity.description: Alternating-least-squares matrix factorization for IMPLICIT feedback (clicks, plays, purchases — not ratings). Factorizes the user-item interaction matrix into low-rank user and item latent-factor matrices under the Hu-Koren-Volinsky confidence weighting, where unobserved cells are weak negatives, then ranks items per user by latent-factor dot product.

dtypes: nonnegative implicit-feedback counts/strengths (sparse CSR, users x items)
consumes.note: no target column exists — the matrix IS both input and supervision; confidence c_ui = 1 + alpha*r_ui is derived from the raw interaction value

emits.note: user latent-factor vector, one per interaction-matrix row; consumable downstream as features via embedding->features:tabular adapter
the item factor matrix as fitted knowledge — the other half of the factorization; item-item similarity queries read from it
recommend(user) returns the top-N (item, score) pairs where score = user_factor . item_factor. `score` understates the real shape: a VARIABLE-LENGTH RANKED LIST per user, not one scalar per row.

factors.note: latent dimensionality of both factor matrices

alpha.note: confidence scaling in c_ui = 1 + alpha*r_ui (HKV); interacts with the raw-count scale of the input matrix

random_state.note: set by the harness for reproducibility; factor init is random otherwise

invariances.why: confidence is LINEAR in the raw interaction value (c_ui = 1 + alpha*r_ui), so rescaling counts rescales the weighted-least-squares weights and changes the factorization (only exactly compensable by rescaling alpha)
log/BM25 weighting of play counts changes the confidence weights and therefore the fit — it is a deliberate modeling choice, not a no-op

unobserved cells are not missing data — the HKV objective sums over ALL user-item cells treating absent entries as zero-preference with confidence 1; sparsity is the native input and imputation has no meaning
the only inputs are two categorical id spaces (users, items) carried as matrix indices; the id->contiguous-index mapping is bookkeeping owned by the wrapper, not a statistical encoding
confidence-weighted least squares on a bilinear form; no likelihood or error distribution is assumed (contrast probabilistic MF variants)
an entity's factor quality scales with ITS OWN interaction count; users/items with a handful of interactions get factors dominated by the regularization prior — the cold-start regime
an entity absent at fit time has NO factor vector at all — scoring is confined to the fitted user/item index spaces and the span of the learned latent space

featureStats.why: the objective's personalization signal lives in observed cells; density so low that most entities have near-zero interactions makes factors indistinguishable from the regularization prior
the share of users/items below ~5 interactions bounds the population the model can rank meaningfully — feeds the cold-start gate and the popularity-fallback share
linear confidence in raw counts lets blockbuster items dominate the least-squares weights; heavy tail flags log/BM25 confidence weighting upstream

modelMetrics.why: a factorization that cannot beat always-recommend-most-popular is not learning personalization — the commit-to-popularity signal, the recommendation analogue of the GBT-vs-linear gap
over-regularized or popularity-dominated factors recommend only the catalog head; coverage is the diversity lens that ranking metrics computed per-user miss

edgeCases.condition: cold-start: user or item with ZERO interactions at fit
edgeCases.behavior: no factor vector exists — the entity cannot be scored at all
edgeCases.note: THE defining edge case; the gate routes cold entities to a popularity/content fallback rather than erroring

edgeCases.condition: user present at fit but new interactions arrive afterward
edgeCases.behavior: stale factors under-rank the new taste
edgeCases.note: implicit exposes recalculate_user() for fold-in; full refresh on schedule

edgeCases.condition: explicit ratings fed as implicit counts
edgeCases.behavior: a 1-star rating becomes a weak POSITIVE (any observation raises confidence)
factors collapse to the regularization prior; recommendations degenerate to noise

deps: implicit>=0.7 (compiled native extension: OpenMP wheels; optional CUDA build for GPU) — HEAVY/OPTIONAL sidecar extra, not in the base image
driver.wrapperNeeds: substantial: (1) user/item id <-> contiguous index maps built at fit and persisted with the model, (2) CSR construction from (user, item, strength) interaction triples, (3) predict surface is recommend(userid, user_row, N, filter_already_liked_items=...) — a per-user ranked list, NOT sklearn per-row predict, (4) cold-start guard: refuse/route entities absent from the fitted index maps
driver.threadSafety: fit is OpenMP-parallel (num_threads); recommend is a thread-safe read of the factor matrices

placementClaims.why: unobserved cells ARE the model's weak-negative signal; densifying/imputing zeros just materializes what the confidence weighting already encodes, at catastrophic memory cost
log/BM25 weighting of heavy-tailed raw counts tempers blockbuster dominance in the confidence weights — a real, fit-changing choice (monotone-transform-NOT-invariant)
z-scoring cells destroys sparsity (zeros become nonzero) and the nonnegativity the confidence construction c=1+alpha*r assumes; global rescaling is only ever alpha in disguise
the inputs are already two categorical id spaces carried as matrix indices; the id->index mapping is wrapper bookkeeping, not a pipeline encode stage
